args.prompt: High-end studio portrait. Seamless charcoal paper backdrop with a gentle warm brass-gold glow behind his head and shoulders. Large soft octabox key at 45 degrees camera-left, subtle hair light from behind, crisp catchlights in both eyes. 85mm f/4, eye level. He looks into the lens with one eyebrow slightly raised, a sharp, amused, knowing look in his eyes. Otto, a tall lean man in his mid-50s, long pale face, deep-set grey eyes with sharp, amused, knowing intelligence, heavy dark brows, neatly styled swept-back dark hair flecked with silver at the temples, real unretouched skin with pores and fine lines; an ENORMOUS charcoal-black handlebar moustache, impeccably groomed and waxed, real individual hair strands, sweeping out and twisting into precise, symmetrical, upturned Dali-esque curls with tightly waxed needle-thin tips, completely covering his mouth; wearing a tailored black fine-gauge turtleneck under a sharply cut dark charcoal wool blazer, a deep oxblood silk pocket square, and a small vintage brass director's viewfinder hanging on a thin brass chain at his chest. Head-and-shoulders, centred, square frame, eyes on the upper third, the whole moustache well inside the frame with margin on both sides. Editorial magazine cover portrait, Vanity Fair or GQ, Salvador Dali meets Tom Ford: luxurious, precise, charismatic, not creepy. True-to-life skin texture, unbranded, no text, no logos.
